questions.text: What does encapsulation in OOP mean?
options: Hiding the implementation details of a class
Allowing multiple inheritance
Using getter and setter methods
Creating a new class from an existing one
questions.explanation: Encapsulation is the concept of hiding the internal details of an object from the outside world and only exposing necessary information through public methods.

questions.text: How does Python handle method overriding in a multi-level inheritance scenario?
options: It calls the method from the most specific class
It calls the method from the least specific class
It calls the method from the current class's parent
It fails and raises an error if multiple inheritance is involved
questions.explanation: Python handles method overriding in a multi-level inheritance scenario by using the method resolution order (MRO) to resolve the call, and it calls the method from the most specific class.

questions.text: How does Python's super() function work in a multi-level inheritance scenario?
options: It calls the method from the most specific class
It calls the method from the least specific class
It calls the method from the current class's parent
It fails and raises an error if multiple inheritance is involved
questions.explanation: Python's super() function works by calling the method from the current class's parent class, and when using multiple inheritance, it will call the method from the next class in the method resolution order (MRO).

questions.text: What is the order in which Python resolves method calls in a multi-level inheritance scenario?
options: From most specific class to least specific class
From least specific class to most specific class
Using a priority queue to resolve the call
Failing and raising an error if multiple inheritance is involved
questions.explanation: Python's method resolution order (MRO) determines the order in which method calls are resolved, and in a multi-level inheritance scenario, it uses C3 linearization to resolve the call, which is roughly from most specific class to least specific class.

questions.text: What is the difference between dynamic method binding and static method dispatch in Python?
options: Dynamic method binding is when a method is called before it is defined, while static method dispatch is when a method is called after it is defined
Dynamic method binding is when a method is called after it is defined, while static method dispatch is when a method is called before it is defined
Dynamic method binding is used for method overriding, while static method dispatch is used for method overloading
Dynamic method binding is used for method overloading, while static method dispatch is used for method overriding
questions.explanation: Dynamic method binding in Python is used for method overriding, where the method to be called is determined at runtime based on the type of the object, while static method dispatch is used for method overloading, where the method to be called is determined at compile time based on the method signature.
